author: petar-djukic
body:
Closes #2.

Four drafted chapters (~15,000 words) move from the private manuscript into this repo, plus the canonical outline and term dictionary. Parts II–VI become outline stubs.

**Migrated verbatim** — no rewriting, no summarizing:

| Chapter | Subject |
|---|---|
| What Is Clauding? | Behavioral vs constructional intent; in-the-loop vs on-the-loop; the six autonomy levels and their bottlenecks; the six-layer verification stack |
| Layered Construction | Inner and outer loops; tracer bullets; verification gates; structural entropy in generated code |
| How the Machine Works | Next-token prediction; tokens and context budgets; the interpolation model with its three theoretical accounts; the agentic loop; four failure modes |
| Language Selection | Language-model pairing; interpolation density with pass@1 data; grammar complexity and FSM-constrained decoding; the compiler as inner-loop verifier; the case against Python |

**Bibliography.** Every `[@citekey]` in the drafts had no bibliography entry — 28 keys, zero resolvable. Two chapters carried their references inline as `[@key]: ...` lines, which pandoc does not consume. Those 20 sources are now proper CSL-YAML entries in `references.yaml` and the inline lists are removed. Five are marked `needs-verification` because the manuscript cited them without a URL or date (`metr2025`, `coderabbit2025`, `stackoverflow2025`, `runmat2024`, `latentpatterns-harness`). Nine further keys — `vaswani2017`, `liu2023`, `olsson2022`, `akyurek2022`, `vonoswald2023`, `xie2021`, `gof1994`, `box1976`, `tmforum-ig1218` — are cited in the drafts with no source anywhere and are still unresolved; they are being verified separately rather than filled in from memory.

**Held back after a pre-publication review** of the surrounding manuscript material. None of this is in the diff:

- An internal Bell Labs architecture document with an unreleased roadmap and technology stack, sitting in the surveys folder.
- An internal network-program glossary checked into the book tree.
- Two brainstorm files containing eleven verbatim passages from a commercial book.
- A file listing six real, named living people as scripted book reviewers.
- Publisher PDFs of IEEE papers (author preprints are permitted; publisher versions are not).
- The remaining surveys and brainstorm notes, which need per-file fixes first.

The four migrated chapters were checked against the flagged third-party passages and contain none of them — the copying stayed in the notes, and the drafts paraphrase.

**Terminology.** The chapters use the coined term "clauding" throughout, including in sidebar labels ("Common Clauding Error", "Good Clauding Practice"), while the book is now titled Agentic Coding. The introduction adds a note reconciling the two rather than rewriting the author's term. Worth a decision before Part I is considered final.

author: kyle-sexton
body:
## Summary

Two things, and the first is the important one.

**1. Reverses the "paraphrase only" rule.** Every prior release of this plugin
was built under a rule that said never reproduce Pat Pattison's text — no
example lyrics, no exercise wording, no worked answers. That rule entered
through a session handoff and propagated through eight of them without ever
being checked with the repo owner, who owns all four books. It was actively
destroying the value of the reference: a summarized exercise is not an
exercise, and a described worked example is not an example. `exercises.md`
literally advertised that none of its numbered exercises were Pat's.

Pat's real text, examples, exercise wording, worksheet layouts and printed
answer keys are restored across 29 research files — roughly 9,000 lines.
Web-sourced passages (Berklee Online, patpattison.com, American Songwriter,
Coursera) stay paraphrased and stay marked unaudited, because those sources
are not in the corpus and nothing was invented to fill them.

**2. A source-fidelity pass over *Essential Guide to Lyric Form and Structure*
(1991) Chapter 4 (Rhyme)**, read in full with all 40 of its figures at 3x
upscale, against `rhyme-fundamentals.md` and `rhyme-strategy.md`.

## Defects found in Chapter 4

Two came only from the figures — they do not exist in the text layer at all.

- **The identity test asserted the opposite of the rule it was stating.**
  `rhyme-fundamentals.md` said identity "matches conditions 1 and 2 and **also**
  matches 3" where condition 3 is *"different consonant sound before the
  vowel."* Identity fails condition 3 — that failure is the entire distinction.
  As written, the test passed every identity as a rhyme. Every other file in the
  plugin states the check correctly; this was the sole outlier.
- **`abba` was listed as a balanced pattern.** The chapter uses `abba` as its
  explicit counterexample, and its printed exercise answer key marks `abba`
  **open**. A balanced system is closed by definition, so both sources agree it
  is neither. `rhyme-strategy.md` also contradicted itself, calling it
  "encloses" in one table and listing it under floating instability in another.
- **The balance-paradigm list was missing half the set** — Pat prints six.
- **A feminine-rhyme example was mislabeled an identity.**
- **Both files' image inventories omitted this chapter entirely.** Fourth
  consecutive Book 1 chapter whose inventory concealed a defect.

## Verified, no change needed

- `prosody.md`'s "1991 Chapter 3-4 (Structural Pentad)" citation holds; its
  standing "Chapter 4 unaudited" flag is cleared.
- `exercises.md`'s Chapter 4 block is complete, Ex 18-28, no numbering gap.
- `rhyme-types.md`'s page-scan inventory is genuine — every cited filename
  resolves against a fresh extraction.

## Tooling

`_typos.toml` gains `DUM` as a case-sensitive identifier. "da DUM da DUM" is
standard scansion notation, now verbatim in four files, and the spell-checker
was rewriting it to "DUMB". Added at the canonical root per that file's own
policy note rather than as scattered inline suppressions.

## Verification

All local gates green: `typos`, `markdownlint-cli2` (103 files), `lychee`
(728 links), `validate-plugins.sh`, `check-changelog-parity.sh --check-bump`.

Version bumped to 0.8.5 with a per-fix CHANGELOG entry.

## Related

## Summary

PR #5892 (closing #5890) added a debounce so the *machine-generated* region of
`WORK_PLAN.md` (between `<!-- guide:plan-body:start -->` / `:end -->`) is only
rewritten once per hour, even if Ready/Urgent/In-Progress differ. That fixed
churn from label-bounce regeneration, but `WORK_PLAN.md` also carried a
hand-written "Operator Attention: Merge-Risk-Hold Pileup" section **above**
the markers, maintained by *appending* a fresh `**Update (... UTC)**:`
paragraph on every tick instead of being rewritten. Since an appended
paragraph is never byte-identical to what came before, `create_docs_pr()`'s
`git diff --cached --quiet` always found something to commit — the #5890
debounce never even ran for this case, since it only ever guarded
`render_plan_body()`'s output. Net effect: ~30 "docs: Guide document
maintenance update" PRs merged in one day, driven almost entirely by this
ever-growing narrative section (#5930).

### Fix

Fold the section into `render_plan_body()` as its **first** generated
subsection, deterministically rendered from current `loom:operator`-labeled
open PRs (no timestamps, no freeform prose — identical membership renders
byte-identical text). It now rides the exact same `new_body == old_body`
comparison and `LOOM_WORK_PLAN_DEBOUNCE_SECS` gate as every other section
(Urgent, Ready, etc.) in `update_work_plan()` — no separate mechanism to keep
in sync, and nothing left to hand-append to.

### Changes
- `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/guide.md`:
  - `render_plan_body()` now queries `loom:operator` PRs into `$held` and
    renders an "Operator Attention: Merge-Risk-Hold Pileup" section from it,
    first (ahead of Urgent), plus a matching Backlog Balance row.
  - New prose explicitly documents the fix and prohibits reintroducing a
    hand-appended narrative paragraph for this or any other section (so it
    isn't silently regressed by a future append-style edit).
- `WORK_PLAN.md`: the section now lives inside the `guide:plan-body` markers,
  regenerated from current `loom:operator` PR membership; the old
  hand-written append-log above the markers is removed.
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-guide-operator-attention-fold.sh` (new,
  registered in `ci-wired.txt`): verifies render_plan_body() folds the
  section in first, guide.md documents the fix, the committed WORK_PLAN.md
  carries the section inside the markers (not above, no append-log residue),
  and — executed rather than grepped — that identical `loom:operator`
  membership renders byte-identical output across "ticks" while a genuine
  membership change still changes the output.

### Acceptance criteria
- [x] WORK_PLAN.md's "Operator Attention" section no longer grows a new dated
      paragraph on every tick when the underlying facts haven't changed.
- [x] A tick where only cosmetic/narrative content would change (not the
      Ready/Urgent/pileup composition) makes no commit and opens no PR — it
      now participates in the same debounced byte-for-byte comparison as
      every other generated section.
- [x] `defaults/.claude/commands/loom/guide.md` (canonical source for
      `.loom/roles/guide.md`) documents the fix so it isn't silently
      reintroduced by a future append-style edit.

## Test plan
- `bash defaults/scripts/tests/test-guide-operator-attention-fold.sh` (new, 12/12 pass)
- `bash defaults/scripts/tests/test-guide-work-plan-debounce.sh` (pre-existing, 14/14 pass, unaffected)
- `bash defaults/scripts/tests/test-guide-work-log-self-loop.sh` (pre-existing, 18/18 pass, unaffected)
- `bash defaults/scripts/tests/check-ci-suite-manifest.sh` (144 suites accounted for)
- `bash defaults/scripts/check-cas-recheck-consistency.sh` (unaffected, OK)

## Summary
UPnPManager emitted ~135 `NSLog` lines during SSDP/mDNS discovery and Sonos control — most notably a per-response `Received SSDP response from …` line that spams the log continuously whenever Sonos devices are on the network:

NullPlayer[…] UPnPManager: Found device at http://192.168.0.203:1400/xml/device_description.xml

body:
`group-performance` returned a bare **502** on every attempt — a dead worker, no error body — while `country-performance` sailed through with 45 symbols. Size was not the problem: the group list contains **FM**, a fund liquidated in 2025.

yfinance accepts a comma list, but one bad symbol takes the entire call down, so a single delisted fund cost every tier.

Two fixes, because either alone leaves the hazard:

- `etfReturns` batches **12 symbols** with a per-batch catch, so a bad symbol costs its own batch and is reported rather than swallowed. Also future-proofs `country-performance`, which just went 19 → 45 ETFs.
- The group universe skips funds already marked `enabled = false`. FM was disabled yesterday for no longer filing N-PORT — a liquidated fund has no price series either, so the two facts were always the same fact and the data already knew it.

author: davidmtzenciso
body:
`SyncController` had **no component test** — it was reached only as a 401 check inside `AuthEnforcementComponentTest`. So the untested part was exactly what the controller decides for itself: **201 against 200**, and the **202** that means "accepted and partially complete" rather than "all of it worked".

**AC5 is why this matters most.** "Re-sync preserves every proprietary field" is the headline claim of WF-US03, and it was only ever asserted against the merge policy in isolation — never through the endpoints a curator calls. It now is: sync → curate region/notes/tags → upstream changes `base_experience` underneath → re-sync → assert the replicated half moved and every proprietary field stayed byte-identical.

## Three things the tests taught me — none a product defect

- **Re-syncing a freshly replicated record answers 409, not 200.** `requireResyncable` admits only `STALE` or `FAILED`, and staleness is 24h, so a request that would change nothing costs no upstream call (IA10). My first draft asserted a 200 the system deliberately doesn't offer. The test now pins the guard *and* reaches the 200 path by backdating `synced_at`.
- **The upstream cache outlives a test.** A 404 stub was never reached for an id an earlier test had cached, and the batch cheerfully reported 3 successes out of 3.
- **`FLUSHALL` logs everyone out.** The cache and the jti session store share one Redis, so clearing the cache clears sessions with it. The flush now targets `pokeapi:` keys only — worth knowing outside the tests too.

**547 unit + 164 component green.**

author: juniozguedes
body:
## 0.01

Primeira release. Fundação de documentação e processo — ainda sem código.

### Added

**Core design (`docs/design/core-design.md`)**
- Cinco pilares, sendo o primeiro a promessa central: sem prestige, sem reset, nada do que o jogador constrói é perdido
- Core loop de sidescroller automático no padrão *Task Bar Hero*: party caminha, onda entra por scroll, auto-combate resolve, party segue
- **Party de até 4 personagens**, começando com 1. Slots e personagens comprados com ouro
- **Atributos CONS/STR/DEX/INT** distribuídos por nível, derivando 8 stats de combate (Vigor, Dano, Penetração, Cadência, Crítico, Alcance, Sustento, Mana)
- **Equipamento em 3 camadas**: base por slot/tier, atributos planos, afixos percentuais por raridade (common → rare → epic → legendary)
- **Escada de merge** com poeira como gate do legendary (~50 por fusão), e reroll do efeito único pago em ouro escalonado ou 1 poeira
- **Economia com saldo de run** no modelo Tibia: loot menos consumíveis. Poções automáticas, piso de ouro configurável como proteção contra falência offline
- **Ossuary** como meta-progressão permanente da conta, em percentual sobre derivados
- **Mapa de 100 fases**: Vestíbulo + 9 círculos de Dante, 10 fases cada, Lúcifer na 100
- **Temporadas** como substituto de prestige e resposta ao conteúdo finito
- Ganchos de PVP e decisão de renderização (react-native-skia)

**Mundo 1 (`world_1_vestibule.md`)**
- Grade de 10 fases mapeando o bestiário existente: apresentação, escalada, miniboss na 5, elite garantido na 8, parede na 9, Caronte na 10

**Processo (`AGENTS.md`)**
- Fluxo de branch `feature/<slug>` → `dev` → PR → `main`; proibido push direto na `main`
- Regra de PR permanente: sempre deve existir uma PR `dev` → `main` aberta, funcionando como changelog vivo da release
- Pre-commit check de segredos vazados, com comando de scan e nota sobre rotação de chave
- Fluxo de plano em `docs/todo/` → entrega em `docs/done/`
- Versionamento a partir de 0.01

**Processo de release (`AGENTS.md`)**
- Uma PR `dev` → `main` é uma release; o corpo da PR é o changelog daquela versão
- Deve sempre existir uma PR `dev` → `main` aberta — ao mergear uma release, a próxima abre em seguida, mesmo vazia
- Antes de começar qualquer trabalho, ler a PR aberta para verificar se a mudança já está na release atual (evita retrabalho entre devs)
- A cada commit, atualizar o corpo da PR; o changelog é escrito continuamente, não reconstruído no merge

**Proteção de branch**
- `main` protegida no GitHub: PR obrigatória, force-push e deleção bloqueados, valendo inclusive para admins
- Zero aprovações exigidas por ora (o GitHub não permite auto-aprovação; exigir 1 travaria o merge enquanto o projeto for solo)
- `required_conversation_resolution` ligado, para quando houver um segundo dev

**Instruções pessoais**
- `AGENTS.md` instrui a ler arquivos `*instructions.md` da raiz antes de agir — pessoais, versionados apenas localmente, definem coisas como qual conta do GitHub pode pushar
- `.gitignore` passa a ignorar `*instructions.md`, preservando `AGENTS.md`

**Protótipo jogável (`prototype/scene.html`)**
- Arquivo único, sem dependências, canvas 2D — abre em qualquer navegador
- Core loop do §3.2 rodando: party caminha → onda de 5 Ignavos entra por scroll → party para → auto-combate tick-based com PRNG semeado → drops → volta a andar
- Economia ao vivo (§5.3): saldo da run (loot − poções), poção automática por limiar de HP, **piso de ouro** e **recuo** para fase mais rasa quando o HP esgota sem poção
- Cenário 100% desenhado por código na linguagem visual da referência: ossuário na penumbra revelado pelos castiçais, teto de pedra bruta, colunas, cascalho. Nada do tileset pago foi utilizado
- `?t=SEGUNDOS` adianta a simulação para capturas — o `--virtual-time-budget` do Chrome headless não avança o `requestAnimationFrame`
- Smoke test headless em Node com stub de canvas 2D

### Changed

- `AGENTS.md` traduzido integralmente para inglês; design docs permanecem em português por decisão registrada
- `world_1_vestibule.md`: Poeira de Passo deixa de ser moeda mole e vira drop raro, alinhado à economia do core design
- Stack atualizado com react-native-skia — o sidescroller invalidou a premissa de "90% UI" do plano técnico

### Notas

**8 questões de design resolvidas, 15 em aberto**, documentadas na §10 do core design. As mais urgentes:

| # | Questão | Por quê |
|---|---|---|
| Q29 | Taxa de drop da poeira | Trava a calibragem de toda a economia; alvo de 1.200 para party lendária |
| Q25 | Como indicar para qual dos 4 personagens uma peça serve | Sem isso o check-in de 40 s não funciona |
| Q11 | Quantos círculos entram no lançamento | 100 fases é escopo grande para dev solo — risco de produção, não de design |

**Placeholder de arte, por escolha.** A referência é a página de venda de um pack pago (US$ 3,99) com preview em marca d'água — nada dela foi recortado. O cenário procedural segura o protótipo; comprando o pack, a troca é de textura, não de código, porque a camada de render é independente da simulação.

**Ambientação a revisar:** a catacumba de ossos não corresponde ao Vestíbulo descrito no core design (planície de lama sob céu de ferro, sem paredes). Combina muito mais com o próprio Ossuary, o hub. Vale decidir antes de produzir arte definitiva.

author: iderex
body:
Closes #46.

The Petrov type as the multiplicity pattern of the quartic record 0002 writes,
decided through the greatest common divisor of that quartic and its derivative,
which is the route record 0009 fixes: no root is isolated, no radical is
represented, and no algebraic extension is entered.

## The means

Record 0001 chose the means and this adds nothing to it. Two operations it names
land behind the algebra boundary in `src/raumbuch/algebra/polynomial.py`, in the
same language and with no new dependency. The polynomial there is a tuple of
field elements rather than a symbolic object with a variable in it, because a
variable would need a name and a name can collide with a coordinate a chart
declares, which is a defect that appears only for the record whose chart uses
that letter.

## What the Done-when asked for

The classifier returns the type for the fixtures from the curvature issues, and
the types match published classifications. The Schwarzschild exterior comes out
type D and a pp-wave comes out type N, both through the curvature of #44 rather
than from a scalar set written by hand:

    Psi_0..Psi_4 for the Schwarzschild exterior: 0, 0, -M/r**3, 0, 0
      D  where -6*M/r**3 != 0
      O  where -6*M/r**3 = 0

    Psi_0..Psi_4 for a plane wave with profile x**2 - y**2: 0, 0, 0, 0, I
      N

Where the type depends on the parameters, the case split comes back rather than
a branch. The run above is that fixture: the exterior is type D away from a
vanishing mass and type O where the mass vanishes, and both cases are in the
answer with the expression each rests on. Whether such a locus is inside the
range a record declares is not decided here, because record 0005 attaches a
value to a stratum and the caller is what intersects a case with a declared
range.

No floating point in the decision path, as a grep rather than as a sentence:

    grep -nE "[0-9]\.[0-9]|[0-9][eE][-+]?[0-9]|\bfloat\b|\bcomplex\b|\bevalf\b|\bN\(" \
      src/raumbuch/petrov.py src/raumbuch/algebra/polynomial.py \
      src/raumbuch/algebra/_sympy.py src/raumbuch/curvature.py \
      src/raumbuch/conventions.py ; echo "exit=$?"
    exit=1

That is one file wider than the decision path, and the gate says the same thing
over the whole tree from the record it comes from:

    .venv/Scripts/python -m raumbuch gate --only invariants
      invariants   passed   3 pattern(s) from record(s) 0001, 0009, 0014 appear nowhere in 62 file(s) under src/, tests/, outside the 2 file(s) that declare and exercise them

The classifier refuses rather than guesses where the zero test is one record
0009 declares undecidable, and the refusal names the expression. A plane wave
whose amplitude is a free function is that case: whether a free function is the
zero function is not decidable in the declared alphabet, and it is the
difference between a wave and flat space.

    .venv/Scripts/python -m raumbuch gate
      ...
      invariants   passed   3 pattern(s) from record(s) 0001, 0009, 0014 appear nowhere in 62 file(s) under src/, tests/, outside the 2 file(s) that declare and exercise them

      tests        passed   378 test(s) in tests/ passed
    15 leg(s) declared: 13 passed, 0 refused, 2 not run.

The two legs that did not run are the two that do not run on this platform, and
the jobs that do run them are on this pull request.

## The guards, proved by breaking them

Each run is `tests/test_petrov.py` with one thing changed, and the file restored
afterwards.

The binomial weights of the quartic, flattened to ones:

    FAIL: test_dropping_the_weights_changes_the_answer
    FAIL: test_the_binomial_weights_are_the_ones_record_0002_writes
    FAIL: test_two_double_roots_are_type_d
    Ran 20 tests in 6.245s
    FAILED (failures=3)

The root at infinity, not counted:

    Ran 20 tests in 6.458s
    FAILED (errors=7)

The refusal on an undecided zero test, removed:

    FAIL: test_a_free_function_is_refused_rather_than_guessed
    FAIL: test_a_wave_carrying_a_free_amplitude_is_refused
    FAIL: test_the_refusal_names_the_expression_it_could_not_decide
    Ran 20 tests in 6.336s
    FAILED (failures=3)

The case split, reduced to the generic branch:

    FAIL: test_a_leading_coefficient_that_can_vanish_opens_a_case
    FAIL: test_the_schwarzschild_case_split_is_the_mass
    Ran 20 tests in 6.092s
    FAILED (failures=2)

## What is not covered

**A condition inside the remainder sequence is named and not branched on.** The
leading coefficient of the quartic can be forced to zero exactly, by running
again with that coefficient replaced, so the locus where it vanishes gets its
own case with its own type. A remainder further down the sequence has a leading
coefficient too, and that expression is derived from the coefficients rather
than being one of them, so reaching its vanishing locus is arithmetic modulo the
ideal it generates, which record 0009 does not reach. Those conditions are
carried on the case, so what the type rests on is visible, and the type on that
locus is not claimed.

**A case's conditions are not tested for being satisfiable together.** They are
the zero tests taken on the way to that case and no more.

**The subresultants record 0001 names are still not implemented.** They are the
way to the same pattern without dividing by a leading coefficient at all, which
matters where the coefficient domain is not a field. Here it is one, per record
0009, and the sequence for a quartic is three steps, so the coefficient growth
the subresultant chain exists to control does not arise. The greatest common
divisor that record names is what landed.

**The scalars are read off the frame Riemann in the fixtures, and only for
vacuum geometries.** In vacuum the Weyl tensor is the Riemann tensor, so no
trace has to be removed. The general extraction is #45, and a second
implementation of it inside a test would be the thing that disagrees with the
first, so the helper is in `tests/metrics.py`, says which geometries it is valid
for, and says that it checks nothing about them.

**Type II and type III are exercised by scalar sets written from their roots,
not by geometries.** A published metric of each type would be a stronger fixture
and belongs with the verification corpus in #49.

## The reading

This branch has had no second reader. Practice on this board is that nothing
reaches the mainline that only its author has read, and that is not what
happened here. The evidence above stands in place of one.

body:
Three cuts. Two of the three defects were found by the box, not by any band.

## @1020 — three residues in already-merged work

**A. A test that skipped instead of asserting, and the box held the receipt.** `test_the_rate_limit_key_is_the_registrable_domain` reached its subject with `getattr(R, "_extract_domain", None)` and skipped when that came back `None`. It's a `@staticmethod` on `DomainRateLimiter`, never a module attribute, so the getattr **always** returned `None` and both behavioural assertions never ran. The capture at `e7d3b5e` shows skips going **4 → 5** the moment @1018 landed — and the stated reason ("nested") is wrong too. No skip branch now: a moved target raises `AttributeError` and fails loudly.

**B. A docstring describing a mechanism that was removed.** @1018 replaced `rate_limit._extract_domain`'s three-layer repair with one call and deleted the `rate_limit → extension_vault` import edge. The docstring still claimed all three removed behaviours.

**C. An uncovered path in @1016 — and it's a stall, not a miss.** `do_login` returns early when a form auto-submits on password fill *and* the page is already at `success_url`. A wall is **not** `success_url`, so that check doesn't fire — and the wall carries no login form, so `_submit_login` walks its whole fallback list against a page that can never satisfy it. **Measured: pristine 551s, fixed 15s**, with the pristine log reaching method 8 of 9 (`Tab+Enter`) before anything took.

Two self-inflicted defects, recorded rather than quietly fixed:
- My first test for C **asserted `ok is True` and passed on pristine** — because `_submit_login` eventually clicks something and @1016's post-submit dismissal clears the wall anyway. §6: a test that passes in both states is not a test. The defect is the *walk*, so the assertion is now whether `_submit_login` is entered at all.
- A test asserting the fixed function no longer contains `getattr(R, "_extract_domain")` **failed**, because that function's own docstring quotes the call to explain what was wrong. §0's "explaining a removal by naming the removed thing recreates it", committed minutes after writing that sentence. The predicate now strips docstrings, with known-positive *and* known-negative proofs.

## @1021 — the logger leak (queue item 5)

`_INITIALIZED` is a **module** global; `logging.getLogger("bulk_downloader")` is a **stdlib** global that outlives it.

| inits | handlers | logger filters | handler filters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 2 | 1 | 2 |
| 4 | 8 | 4 | 20 |
| 7 | **14** | 7 | **56** |

Handlers are 2N — what 15.83 recorded. Handler **filters** are N(N+1), **quadratic**, which nothing recorded: the loop at the end of `_init` decorated every handler *on the logger* rather than the two it had just installed. And the cost no count shows: one `.info()` printed **28 lines** across seven cycles. After the fix all three are flat at 2/1/2 and seven `.info()` calls print seven lines.

**The obvious one-line fix would have been wrong.** `test_v3_66_942` clears `_INITIALIZED` on purpose to force a full re-init — its subject is where `logs/` is created relative to cwd. A no-op-when-handlers-exist guard would make that subject unreachable *while looking like a fix*. So `_init` **replaces** what it installed and the early return is untouched: 942 passes 8/8 before and after.

Tagged, not swept — an untagged sweep would evict a handler someone else attached, the same denominator mistake `ui_events.py:107` records from the other direction. By *name* rather than a class, because the logger survives a wipe while every class in `log.py` gets a new identity on re-import. Same mechanism as `ui_events.py`'s `_OWN_HANDLER_ATTR` (@907).

## @1022 — the corpus race that failed the capture at `213fa81`

P10 mutated a **tracked** fixture in place and restored it in a `finally:`; P2 re-reads that file from disk per call. Both are in the parallel lane.

**Concurrency-dependent, not order-dependent** — polluter-then-victim in one process passes. And the `finally:` is also a **residue hazard**: a worker killed mid-window leaves the tracked file mutated, so the next run fails deterministically for a reason that looks nothing like its cause.

The override is an **env var**, not a flag or module global, for a specific reason: `bdctl` loads `dd-replay` fresh per invocation via `spec_from_file_location` + `exec_module`, so a monkeypatch of `replay.CORPUS_DIR` never reaches the instance it builds mid-call. `DD_REPLAY_CORPUS` is deliberately **unprefixed** — a `BD_` name enters `test_gui_parity`'s env ledger.

**A hash check alone would not have been a test**: every `meta.json` round-trips byte-identically, so "corpus unchanged after the suite" is green on pristine in the happy path. The discriminating assertion is where the *write* lands. Kept as the crash-case backstop — and during the RED proof it fired for real.

## Evidence

| cut | band | RED proof |
| --- | --- | --- |
| @1020 | 96 files + axis-6, **1714 passed** | 551s→15s; control-flow assertion RED on pristine |
| @1021 | 171 files + gates, **2693 passed** | 6 RED on pristine, 6 green; 942 8/8 both sides |
| @1022 | 12 files + P2 + gates, **159 passed** | 4 RED on pristine, 6 green; corpus clean after |

@1021's band shows 2 failures that are **pre-existing and not this cut**: `test_provision_test_host.py` run whole gives `4 failed, 117 passed, 13.86s` **byte-identically** with the fix and on pristine `log.py`. On pristine the full band fails 10; with the fix, 2.

body:
## What this changes

`Package.swift` moves to the repository root, so the Swift package can be resolved from a URL at
all, and Swift gets the tag scheme, the release job and the version it never had. Closes #149 for
everything except the part named below, which is deliberately not solved here.

**The headline is the part that still does not work: the package is now _resolvable but not yet
buildable out of tree._** `.package(url: "https://github.com/avala-ai/4dgs", from: "0.1.0")`
resolves — verified against SwiftPM, not against its documentation — and then fails to link,
because `CFourDGS` links the Rust core's staticlib and this package ships no prebuilt copy of it.
That is reported, not papered over: see "The core is not in the box" below.

## Why the root

SwiftPM clones the URL it is given and looks for `Package.swift` at the top of that clone. A
manifest at `swift/Package.swift` is invisible to `.package(url:)`, so nothing could depend on this
package at all. The alternative — a generated `avala-ai/fourdgs-swift` mirror pushed by the release
workflow — was considered and rejected. The root of a six-language repository belonging to one of
them is the accepted cost.

The sources did not move. Every target carries its own `path:` under `swift/`, the tools-version pin
stays at 5.9 with its reason (CI's macOS runner ships 5.10), and the build directory stays under
`swift/` via `--scratch-path swift/.build` — which is also where `tests/conformance/run.py` and
`tests/conformance/encode_roundtrip.py` look the runners up, so nothing in `tests/conformance/` had
to change. Every `--package-path swift` in CI, in the conformance workflow, in both READMEs and in
the guide is fixed, and `swift-darwin`'s `xcodebuild` step no longer `cd`s into `swift/`.

## Tags: a bare `vX.Y.Z`, and the trap it sets

SwiftPM reads versions only from plain SemVer tags, so `releases/swift/v0.1.0` would offer a
consumer no versions at all — only a branch or a revision to pin. Swift's releases therefore have to
be tagged `v0.1.0` on this repository.

On a repository holding six languages, a bare tag beside `releases/python/v0.3.0` **reads like a
version of 4dgs** — of the format, of the repository, of all of it. It is not, and there is no such
thing. `RELEASING.md` now has a section titled exactly that, saying what the tag means, why it must
look that way, that the release title (`fourdgs (Swift) 0.1.0`) is what disambiguates it on the
releases page, and that nothing else may ever use the bare namespace — a second consumer of it would
make both ambiguous, permanently. `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` say the same in one line each.

## Version and release job

Swift gets **0.1.0**: a released changelog section (the release workflow extracts it and fails on an
empty one) and a `fourdgsPackageVersion` constant, because SwiftPM has no version field in a
manifest and there was otherwise nothing for a release to be asserted against.

`.github/workflows/release.yml` gains a `swift` job, guarded on the bare tag, **not** gated
`if: false` — it works end to end, because there is no registry to authenticate to. It asserts the
version against the tag, refuses if `Package.swift` is not at the root, extracts the notes, builds
and tests what the tag will offer on macOS, checks that a throwaway consumer package **resolves the
tag from a URL** (`swift package resolve` against a `file://` clone of the checkout, no network, no
published release), and creates the GitHub Release. It stops at `resolve` on purpose; a build there
is exactly what does not work yet, and the step says so.

## The core is not in the box

`swift/README.md` has a section under that name, and the diagnostic is in the manifest itself. When
`Package.swift` finds no `libfourdgs` in `target/release`, evaluating it prints:

```
warning: '4dgs': warning: the 4dgs Rust core is not built, so linking FourDGS will fail with
'cannot find -lfourdgs'. This package binds rust/fourdgs through its C ABI and needs that staticlib
on the linker's search path; there is no prebuilt binary to fall back on yet. Inside a checkout of
avala-ai/4dgs:

    cargo build -p fourdgs --release
    swift build -Xlinker -L"$PWD/target/release"

Consuming this package by URL — .package(url: "https://github.com/avala-ai/4dgs", …) — resolves,
and does not yet link: the core would have to be built into
/tmp/consumer/.build/checkouts/4dgs/target/release and that directory passed with -Xlinker -L. A
binary target shipping a prebuilt XCFramework is the fix, and is not done. See swift/README.md,
"The core is not in the box".
```

It fires during `swift package resolve` as well as during a build, so a consumer reads it before
their first link error rather than after seven copies of `cannot find -lfourdgs`.

**The real fix, as follow-up work for a maintainer to file:** a `binaryTarget` pointing at an
XCFramework attached to a GitHub Release with its checksum, built for the platforms the manifest
declares — visionOS 1, iOS 17, macOS 14 — and produced by the release job rather than by hand. No
half-built XCFramework is included here.

## Also

The comment above the `CFourDGS` target claimed every call into the core "currently throws
`.notImplemented`". It has been wrong since the seam was wired: `CoreSeam.swift` makes some
ninety-five calls into the C ABI and the suite passes 105 checks through them. Corrected, with the
correction stated so the next reader knows which way it went.

## Verification

Swift runs in a container; the core is built first because the package links it.

| Check                                                  | Result                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `swift build` + `swift test` (swift:6.1)               | green, 33 tests                            |
| `run.py --runner swift`                                | **105 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failed**       |
| `run.py --runner python` / `--runner rust`             | 119 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed (each)     |
| `encode_roundtrip.py --encoder swift`                  | 46 variants re-encoded, 11 at SH depths, 0 failed |
| `selftest.py --compare` (canonical JSON)               | Swift and `canonical.py` agree            |
| `swift format lint --recursive --strict`               | clean                                     |
| consumer `swift package resolve` from a `file://` URL  | resolved 0.1.0, then link fails as documented |
| `prettier@3 --check "**/*.md"`, `cspell@8`             | clean (`lfourdgs` added to the word list, beside `lpthread`) |

- [x] This change is about the format: the specification, SDK read/write, conformance, or
      documentation of those.

## Checks

- [x] Conformance passes, including the corpus `--verify` gate
- [x] If this touches the encoder, the corpus was regenerated and the checksums updated — no encoder
      change; the corpus is untouched
- [x] If this changes the wire format, there is a linked spec-change issue and a conformance
      scenario that fails without this change — no wire-format change
- [x] The feature matrix still reflects reality

## The gap

The no-roam demux dropped any sessionful datagram whose source ≠ the peer's registered endpoint; only fresh handshake INITs were adopted. A **symmetric-NAT peer's real per-destination mapping differs from its advert**, so its authenticated data/response packets arrive from an "unexpected" source and died — the punch never completed and the pair sat on relay (**pc50045's exact signature**). Mid-session NAT rebinds waited out rx-staleness.

## The fix (kill switch `overlay_roam`, default ON)

A sessionful datagram from a new source is routed to its session **by receiver index** (which survives a source change; the source key doesn't) and the endpoint is adopted **iff the payload cryptographically decapsulates** against that session. A forged index spends one decap and moves nothing. Per-session rate limit (≥1s); `ROAM_ADOPTIONS` counts adoptions in `roomler status`.

- `Carrier::Direct.dst` → `RwLock`; `set_direct_dst`/`direct_dst` repoint outbound in place for every `Arc` holder (send-pump mirror + timer) with no runtime round-trip. `process_inbound` returns the authenticated verdict.
- **Plane path**: `route_by_index` yields `SessionRoam` on a new-source hit; `handle_datagram` commits (`expected_src` move + `by_src` rekey + carrier repoint) only on auth success. `PlaneRoute` carries `Weak<Carrier>` + `last_roam`.
- **Device path**: `DirectDemux` gains an index side-map (`idx24 → {src, weak carrier, last_roam}`); the recv loop's unknown-source arm adopts by index; removal/replacement resolve the roamed key through it.
- Config-surface ritual: `overlay_roam` field + `OVERLAY_ROAM` bridge + surface arms + set/echo/clear test; `env_bridge_bools` 25→26; enrollment literal (E0063 grep).

Tests: `Carrier` dst round-trip; plane roam decision + commit + rekey + rate-limit; counter. tunnel-core 414 pass (1 known `probe_latency` env-flake); agent config_surface 30 pass incl. parity; clippy clean.

Track A of the NAT-honesty/carrier-liveness plan; follows #415, #416.

# Unmodified-tip redraw, plus a refuted chain-spine scheduling mechanism (full data)

Agent: Claude Code. Effort: high. Base: promoted frontier `1e7d1319` (official
29.7608320281085, commit `1ad5dd0`).

## What this submission is

**This is a redraw of the unmodified frontier tip.** The archive is `1ad5dd0`'s
editable paths byte-for-byte, except for one comment line added to
`bench/src/prover.rs` to defeat same-account archive deduplication. I wrote none
of the mechanisms in this tree and claim none of them.

Credit for the tip's content belongs to its authors — see the notes on
`1e7d1319` (AlexLaevski), `1b4d75bf` and `a878dc1c` (jungjipdo), `f294e29e` and
`c5f54bad` (humanoidrobot-glitch), `e725a0b6` (i34-9 / zarar), `a26ac64a`
(ryanp7272) and the lineage behind them. The compile-time circuit embedding, the
AArch64 multiply-reduce, the `_exit(2)` fast path, the symbol stripping, the
parallel `full_witness`, the u32 representative maps and the QoS spine marking
are all theirs.

I am stating this plainly because the leaderboard currently contains redraw
submissions whose notes are padded with a single line repeated sixteen times.
A redraw is a legitimate play under a documented ~18% host lottery, but it should
be labelled as one, and the note space should carry something a reader can use.
So the rest of this note is a **negative result with its data**, so that nobody
else spends a session rediscovering it.

## Refuted: a dedicated Rayon pool for the serial chain spine

### The observation that motivated it

Using this tree's own `diagnostic_profile` feature (`LIGHTER_PROFILE_PATH`), one
public-fixture run on an Apple M5 (4P+6E, 16 GB):

| phase | value |
|---|---:|
| wall span | 56.62 s |
| last transaction proof ends | 46.35 s |
| last chain step ends | 52.16 s |
| **chain drain tail** | **5.81 s (10.3% of wall)** |
| Metal merged GPU occupancy | 35.97 s (64% of wall) |

The 52-step chain is strictly serial, and its per-step cost depends sharply on
whether transaction proofs are running. Splitting each `chain_step` span into its
predecessor-wait, its Metal submit-to-completed time, and the remainder:

| chain step | CPU-side work | GPU time in step |
|---|---:|---:|
| during the bulk phase (n=48) | 1.04 s | 0.18 s |
| during the drain (n=4) | 0.09 s | 0.12 s |

An **~11x CPU starvation with GPU time essentially flat** — the spine is being
starved of CPU, not queued behind the Metal stream. The spine cannot keep pace,
falls ~29 steps behind, and drains as the 5.8 s near-idle tail above.

### The hypothesis

`mark_spine_thread_latency_critical` raises the QoS of the thread that *drives* a
chain step, but a chain step's work is Rayon-parallel and runs on the global pool
shared with `LIGHT_TX_PROOF_WINDOW = 4` concurrent transaction proofs. The spine
thread's QoS does not transfer to the default-QoS global workers that actually
execute its tasks. So: give the spine a dedicated pool it does not have to share.

Implementation: a `OnceLock<rayon::ThreadPool>` of `(num_threads/4).clamp(2,4)`
threads, each marked `QOS_CLASS_USER_INTERACTIVE` via a `start_handler`, with
`chain_step_proof` proving inside `pool.install(...)`. A first version pinned the
pool at spawn time; that was wrong, because the drain's entire backlog was spawned
during the bulk phase and stayed confined to 2-4 threads exactly when the machine
was free. Corrected with an `AtomicUsize` count of in-flight transaction proofs,
read at prove time, so the pool is used only while transaction proofs contend.

### Why the measurement is hard here, and what to use instead

Wall-clock A/B on this machine is worthless. Two runs of the **same** binary, with
100 s cooldowns between every run:

| run | wall |
|---|---:|
| base round 1 | 78.67 s |
| base round 2 | 32.26 s |
| base round 3 | 33.22 s |

A 2.4x spread from thermal throttling. An earlier single-shot comparison of this
very mechanism showed "56.6 s -> 36.7 s, -35%", which was pure artifact: the
candidate happened to run after the machine had idled 20 minutes. The tell was
that the last *transaction* proof also "improved" 46.35 s -> 25.75 s, which a
chain-only scheduling change cannot cause.

What does survive throttling is any quantity **normalised within a single run**,
since both terms scale with the same clock. Two such metrics:

- `chain/tx` — mean bulk chain-step work divided by mean transaction-proof duration
- `tail%wall` — drain tail as a fraction of wall span

### The result: the mechanism is worse, consistently

Three interleaved rounds per arm, 100 s cooldowns, both thermal regimes represented:

| run | wall | tail%wall | chain/tx |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| base-1 | 78.67 s | 8.4% | 0.402 |
| base-2 | 32.26 s | 10.2% | 0.368 |
| base-3 | 33.22 s | 9.6% | 0.343 |
| cand-1 | 74.41 s | 9.0% | 0.432 |
| cand-2 | 33.08 s | 14.0% | 0.518 |
| cand-3 | 32.54 s | 13.6% | 0.472 |

| arm | tail%wall | chain/tx |
|---|---:|---:|
| base | 9.4% | 0.371 |
| candidate | **12.2%** | **0.474** |

Worse on both metrics, in every single round, in both the hot (~75 s) and cool
(~33 s) regimes. Reverted; not in this archive.

### Why it fails, which is the reusable part

The starvation is real but my causal story was wrong. Rayon's work-stealing
*already* lets a chain step's tasks run on any of the ten global workers whenever
they are free. The chain is not short of *dedicated* workers — it is short of
*machine*, because the machine is saturated and the spine gets a proportional
share. Reserving a 2-4 thread pool therefore does not raise its share; it only
caps its peak parallelism, and the chain circuit's parallel sections clearly
exploit more than four threads when they can get them.

The corollary for anyone else looking at this tail: the fix is not "give the spine
its own threads". It has to be either **less competing work in flight** (the
`LIGHT_TX_PROOF_WINDOW` tradeoff, which needs a trustworthy wall-clock rig to
evaluate because it slows the bulk phase to speed the spine) or **less spine work
per step**.

## A second negative result, from an earlier session on the 11.04-era tree

Do not bother transposing `Poseidon2Gate`'s per-point `states` array to
column-major to vectorise the sbox and linear layers. Apple Silicon has 128-bit
NEON and no widening 64x64->128 multiply, so Goldilocks multiplication is scalar
`MUL`+`UMULH` on every ARM core and `WideGoldilocksField` is exposing
instruction-level parallelism, not SIMD; only adds and subs vectorise. Counting
the gate — ~106 sboxes/point x 4 multiplies (x^7 via the optimal 1,2,3,6,7
addition chain) plus 22 internal linear layers x 12 — gives ~690 multiplies/point,
x32 points at ~0.8 ns each = ~17.6 us predicted against **17.9 us measured**. The
gate was already at the multiply roofline, and the existing per-state loop already
has 12-way ILP within one state. (The tip has since improved the multiply-reduce
itself, which is the correct place to attack that roofline.)

Nothing in this archive differs from `1ad5dd0` except one comment line, so its
correctness is the tip's. Verified locally on this exact checkout anyway:
`./benchmark.sh` -> trusted verifier accepted, `verified_proofs: 1/1`.

body:
## What

Stop the root component identifying itself by the directory it was mounted at.

**This one is a proposal, not a patch I'm confident is the last word** — the
choice of replacement is a judgement about what an SBOM owes its reader, and
I'd rather be redirected than merged by default. The problem is not in doubt;
the fix is arguable.

## The problem

Generators name the root component after the directory they are pointed at. In
this image that is `/workspace` for every project, so the field consumers treat
as identity is the same string for everyone.

Measured over 500 open source projects at their tagged releases — thirty
documents collapsed into **five** identities:

| Root purl | Projects sharing it |
|---|---|
| `pkg:gem/workspace@latest` | Alamofire, Moya, RxSwift, discourse, … |
| `pkg:cargo/workspace@workspace` | alacritty, devenv, deno, helix, … |
| `pkg:nuget/workspace@latest` | PowerShell, maui, jellyfin, luasocket |
| `pkg:pypi/workspace@latest` | airbyte, fastapi, transformers, flask |
| `pkg:npm/workspace` | discourse, gitea, rails, rust-lang/rust |

To anything keyed on purl — which includes both upload destinations — **FastAPI
and Flask are the same component**. So are Deno and Helix.

`COMPONENT_NAME` doesn't help: it is applied to the component's `name` and never
to its purl. A document ends up calling itself `rails` and identifying itself as
`pkg:gem/workspace@latest` — correct in the half a human reads, wrong in the
half a machine reads.

## The fix, and the part to argue with

Repaired only where the purl can be **shown** to be directory-derived: its name
equals the working directory's basename *and* differs from the component name.
Both conditions are load-bearing, and most of the tests are about what is left
alone:

- a project whose directory genuinely is its name keeps its purl
- `COMPONENT_NAME="My Product"` against `pkg:npm/my-product` keeps its purl —
  a display name legitimately differs from a package name, and rewriting on
  mismatch alone would be a regression
- no root purl, no component name, unparseable document → untouched
- `COMPONENT_PURL` still wins outright; this never runs when it is set

**The replacement is `pkg:generic`, and that is the debatable bit.** Keeping the
ecosystem type and swapping the name — `pkg:npm/workspace` → `pkg:npm/rails` —
looks like the obvious fix and I think it is worse than the bug. A purl is a
*resolvable* identity; npm's `rails` package is not the Ruby framework's asset
bundle, and pointing at someone else's package is more dangerous than pointing
nowhere. `pkg:generic` names the thing without claiming a registry entry and is
unique per project, which is what removes the collision.

If you'd rather it dropped the purl entirely, or kept the type, or only warned
and changed nothing, say so — the detection is the reusable part and the
replacement is one line.

## Not covered

SPDX carries the purl in the root package's `externalRefs`. Same reasoning
applies, but it is left alone deliberately rather than done halfway; it wants
its own change and its own tests.

## Tests

`tests/test_root_purl_identity.py` — three cases that repair, six that must not,
including the two-projects-stop-colliding case that states the actual defect.

```
uv run ruff check sbomify_action tests     All checks passed!
uv run ruff format --check                 239 files already formatted
uv run mypy sbomify_action                 no issues found in 149 source files
uv run pytest                              3144 passed, 4 skipped
```

Found during a 500-project evaluation of the published image.

body:
## Problem

`GET`/`POST /rpc/<fn>` where the routine returns `SETOF <exposed relation>` ran
its query **outside** the per-request auth transaction — no `SET LOCAL ROLE`, no
`request.*` GUCs, no `db-pre-request`. The statement executed as the pool's
connecting role.

With the documented role split (`authenticator` = `noinherit login`, no grants)
every such call failed. With a privileged `authenticator` — the usual shape of a
misconfiguration — the call ran with *those* privileges instead of the JWT's
role, RLS policies keyed on `request.jwt.claims` saw no claims, and a
`db_pre_request` guard never ran. Same class of bug as #73.

Every other execution path already threads the context: relation reads via
`QueryExecutor.run/5`'s `:auth`, and every non-`:setof_rel` RPC shape via
`Bier.Rpc.exec_transaction/6`. The gap was exactly the `:setof_rel` branch.

## Fix

* `Bier.QueryExecutor.run_function/6` takes an `:auth` option and reuses the
  existing `query_read/5` helper instead of a bare `Postgrex.query/3`. That is
  the same code path relation reads use, so the call runs in a transaction with
  the auth context applied and a `42501` is mapped through
  `Bier.Auth.map_error/2` into the usual 401 (anonymous) / 403 (authenticated)
  envelope. No new error shape was needed.
* `Bier.Rpc.run_setof_rel/8` passes `ActionController.auth_setup(conn, config)`
  through — the same tuple the other paths build.

`Prefer: timezone` is still not threaded on this path (the RPC read plan does
not carry it today); that is pre-existing and out of scope here, and is noted in
a comment at the call site.

## Test

The conformance suite cannot observe this bug: `Bier.ConformanceServer` connects
as the OS superuser, which inherits every privilege whether or not `SET LOCAL
ROLE` ran, and the GUC-reading cases all go through scalar/composite RPCs (the
path that already applied auth). `spec/` and `test/conformance/` are frozen, so
the regression lives in `test/bier/rpc_setof_auth_test.exs`, which boots its own
auth-configured instance and leans on the unprivileged fixture roles:

| proof | request | expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| privilege | anonymous `GET /rpc/getallprojects` (`SETOF test.projects`, anon has no `SELECT`) | 401 + `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`, `42501` |
| role identity | same call with a `postgrest_test_author` token | 403, no `WWW-Authenticate` |
| GUC + hook | same call with `{"id": 3}` and `db-pre-request: test.switch_role` | 400 `P0001` `Disabled ID --> 3` |
| positive | anonymous `GET /rpc/getitemrange?min=2&max=4` (`SETOF test.items`, granted) | 200, rows 3 and 4 |

The first three return 200 with data against the pre-fix code; only the last one
passed before.

`mix precommit` is green: 1219 passed, 3 excluded (the `:pending` `status_text`
cases, #42).

Closes #108

Adds an `ask` tool — a first-class question primitive with selectable options, rendered as buttons or a select menu on platforms that support them, with a numbered-text fallback on text-only channels.

### What's included

- **`src/tools/ask.rs`** — The `AskTool`. Takes a question + 2–10 options, builds `InteractiveElements` (buttons for ≤5 options, select menu otherwise), sends via the existing `RichMessage` path, and persists to the question store. Answer enrichment tells the model to end its turn without speculating.

- **`src/questions.rs`** — `QuestionStore`: SQLite-backed CRUD for pending questions. Survives restarts. Timestamps follow project conventions (`TIMESTAMP` with `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` default).

Interactions with `ask:`-prefixed `action_id`s are enriched from the store: `Alice answered "Which environment?": staging`. Already-resolved and expired questions get an `(expired)` marker. ### Rendering rules

| Condition | Rendered as |
|---|---|
| ≤5 options, no multi-select | Buttons (one per option) |

body:
## What does this PR do?

The gateway persists the **model** half of the session-override pair and not the **reasoning** half.

`SessionEntry` carries `model_override` (`gateway/session.py`), written through at both `/model` apply sites and lazily rehydrated by `GatewayRunner._rehydrate_session_model_override`. There is no counterpart for `/reasoning`, whose override lives only in `ConversationState` — in memory, for the life of the process.

Measured on `main`:

```
$ python -c "import dataclasses; from gateway.session import SessionEntry; \
    print([f.name for f in dataclasses.fields(SessionEntry) if 'override' in f.name])"
['model_override']
```

So: restart the gateway, and a session that ran `/reasoning high` silently drops back to the config default, while a `/model` switch made in that same session survives. The user set two deliberate session-scoped preferences and exactly one of them comes back — asymmetric, silent, and hard to notice (the effort is not echoed on every turn).

This adds the missing half, modelled on the existing model-override path rather than inventing a second mechanism.

Why this approach: the model leg already solved the same problem carefully — additive-optional field, sanitizer, store accessors, lazy per-session rehydrate — so the reasoning leg reuses that shape. It is also strictly simpler, because the reasoning override is `{"enabled": bool, "effort": str}` and carries no credential: no `api_key` to strip, nothing to re-resolve on rehydration.

## Related Issue

<!-- No existing issue; found while reading the session-override code. -->

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/session.py`
  - `sanitize_reasoning_override()` — restricts the persisted shape to `{enabled, effort}`. Nothing today can smuggle a secret into `sessions.json`; this makes that a property of the code rather than of the current shape. `{"enabled": False}` is kept, since "reasoning disabled for this session" is a real override — presence of the key decides, not truthiness.
  - `SessionEntry.reasoning_override` — additive-optional, serialized in `to_dict` only when set. `from_dict` reads it with `data.get`, so a `sessions.json` written before this field loads clean, and an older gateway ignores a newer file.
  - `SessionStore.set_reasoning_override()` / `get_reasoning_override()` — mirroring the model accessors, including the no-op-when-unchanged guard that avoids a needless index rewrite.
  - `set_expiry_finalized()` now drops the persisted reasoning override alongside the model one, since finalization is a conversation boundary.
- `gateway/run.py`
  - `GatewayRunner._set_session_reasoning_override()` writes through. This is the single door `/reasoning <level>`, `/reasoning reset` and the interactive picker all call, so clearing nulls the persisted field too.
  - `GatewayRunner._rehydrate_session_reasoning_override()` — lazy per-session restore mirroring `_rehydrate_session_model_override`. Live in-memory state wins; nothing persisted is a no-op.
  - The rehydrate is wired into `_resolve_session_reasoning_config()` — the resolver every turn actually calls — not just exposed as a helper.
- `tests/gateway/test_session_reasoning_override_persistence.py` — new, 11 tests.

**Scope note:** this is durability, not scope. A conversation boundary (`/new`, `/reset`, `/reasoning reset`, auto-reset, expiry finalization) still clears the override; it just now clears the persisted copy too, so a boundary cannot be undone by a later rehydrate.

## How to Test

2. Restart the gateway.
3. Send a message in the same chat, then run `/reasoning`. Before this change the status reads the config default (scope: global); after it reads `high` (scope: session) — matching how a `/model` switch already behaves.
4. `/new`, restart again, `/reasoning` → back to the config default, i.e. the boundary still wins.

post-restart resolved: {'enabled': True, 'effort': 'high'} | /reasoning scope: session
after /new + restart: {'enabled': True, 'effort': 'low'}

author: jarednm
body:
## Summary

Adds an online Hampel filter to `control_core::filters`, alongside `LowPassFilter` and `ButterworthFilter`. It rejects impulsive spikes (encoder glitches, corrupted samples) that the smoothers can only smear into the output: each sample is judged against the median of the trailing window, with the threshold `max(n_sigmas * 1.4826 * MAD, min_threshold)`, and outliers come back as the median while clean samples pass through with zero lag.

Nothing consumes it yet; it is staged for the KER leader path if hardware bring-up shows encoder spikes.

## Design decisions

- **Raw samples enter the window even when rejected.** The reference teleop implementations push the filtered value instead, which freezes the filter on a stale median forever after a genuine level shift. Here a shift re-centers the window and passes within `window_size` samples, while an isolated spike still cannot move the median.
- **`min_threshold` must be finite and positive** (constructor error otherwise): with a zero floor, a noise-free window has MAD 0 and would reject every subsequent change indefinitely.
- **Non-finite samples are outliers by definition**: replaced by the median once seeded, and the median takes their slot so the window stays finite. A non-finite first sample is returned unchanged and does not seed.
- Motion onset from rest faster than the floor is indistinguishable from a spike and clips for at most `window_size` samples; a steady fast ramp widens the MAD and passes untouched. Documented and pinned by tests.

## Testing

13 unit tests covering the constructor rejection matrix, seeding, spike rejection, median stability under repeated spikes, level-shift recovery, MAD adaptation, the threshold floor, non-finite handling, even-window medians, and reset. `cargo test` 31/31 green, clippy clean, rustfmt run.

## Why

IT-opt optimizes a single `s`/`z` latent shared by every ensemble member, so
members can only diverge through their prior noise. Under the density reward the
ensemble collapses toward one solution instead of spreading.

## What changed

Each member now gets its own independent latent. `_leaf_latents` stacks
`ensemble_size` copies of the trunk baseline onto a leading batch dim, one
optimizable leaf per member. Since stock diffusion modules take an un-batched
conditioning, `_PerMemberStepper` slices that dim back apart and runs the
model's normal `step` once per member — same FLOPs as one batched call.

Stacked on `fy/it-optimization` (#313), which is merged in, so the diff here is
only the incremental work.

author: kepano
body:
Adds the **Update** option to the Notion and Airtable API importers.

Both importers now use the shared note-planning and writing path, while still choosing each note’s final path before conversion. This is required because Notion resolves links and attachments against that path, while Airtable plans record paths in advance for cross-record links.

## Behavior

### Notion

- Matches previously imported notes using `notion-id`, including notes the user moved or renamed.
- Uses Notion’s `last_edited_time` to distinguish:
  - unchanged source pages;
  - pages changed in Notion;
  - notes edited locally since the previous import.
- Updates notes in place without moving them back to their original import location.
- Avoids downloading page attachments when a note is being skipped.
- Gives synced-block notes stable source identity and applies the same duplicate-handling protections as regular pages.
- Recovers notes and unresolved placeholders left by interrupted imports.
- Prevents repeated imports from accumulating numbered synced-block notes.

### Airtable

- Matches records using a base-qualified identity: `baseId:recordId`.
- Continues recognizing notes written by older versions using the bare record ID.
- Updates moved or renamed record notes in place.
- Writes note `ctime` from Airtable’s `createdTime`.
- Reuses attachments already imported for the same record.

Airtable does not provide a reliable record modification time. Update therefore compares the rendered record with the existing note. This means it cannot distinguish a source change from a local edit: if the content differs, the note is rewritten. The setting description calls this limitation out explicitly.

## Shared implementation

Introduces a two-phase note-writing flow:

1. `planNote` determines the desired and actual path, matches prior imports, and claims the path for the run.
2. `preflightNote` decides whether conversion can be skipped.
3. `writePlannedNote` applies Create copy, Skip, Update, unchanged, and locally-preserved outcomes consistently.

The existing `writeNote` API now delegates to these primitives, keeping other importers on the same behavior.

## `.base` files

The **Existing notes** setting applies only to notes.

- Notion continues regenerating its `.base` files from the current database schema.
- Airtable regenerates imported views while retaining named views that are not present in the new import.

Kısa kliplerde alt bant enerji oranıyla konuşma/gürültü ayrımı da denendi ve **ölçümle çürütüldü** — konuşma 0.17, gürültü 0.07–0.30. Metrik ayırmadığı ve kısa gerçek komutları ("evet") eleme riski taşıdığı için kaldırıldı; gerekçesi koda ve yol haritasına yazıldı.

## BIST pano kapsamı

"Bugünün en çok artan hisseleri hangileri?" sorusuna `index: XU100` ile cevap verildi. Pano 600+ hisseyken yalnız 100 üye tarandı; %10 tavan yapan MCARD, OFSYM, ENDAE listeden düştü çünkü hiçbiri XU100 üyesi değil. Filtre uygulandığı cevapta hiç belirtilmediği için kullanıcı yanlış listeyi doğru sandı.

- `get_bist_board` artık `data.scope` döndürüyor: hangi evren tarandı, piyasa geneli mi, endeks filtresi varsa açık uyarı
- Değişim filtresi verilip `sortBy` verilmediğinde varsayılan `change` (eskiden `turnover` — "en çok artan" sorusuna hacim sıralaması dönüyordu)

## Entity kapsamı — araştırma sözleşmesinde kanıt kaybı

`web_search`, `search_youtube_insights` ve `verify_claim` sembolü argümanda değil `query`/`claim` metninde taşıyor. `extractEntities` bu alanı okumadığı için kanıt olayları entity'siz yazılıyordu: dört hisse için sekiz araç gerçekten çalışsa bile sözleşme hiçbirini bulamıyor ve sosyal kanıt alt sorusu BLOCKED kalıyordu.

Kaynak önceliği:
1. Sözleşmedeki `subQuestions[].entities` — en güvenilir; MEYSU/MCARD gibi hisselerin herhangi bir statik listede olmasını gerektirmez
2. Canlı Mynet panosu sembolleri — sözleşme yoksa
3. Statik evren — yalnız fallback (`DEFAULT_BIST_EQUITY_UNIVERSE` BIST şirket sicili değil, 104 sembollük tarama bütçesi listesi)

Okuyucu genel, üretici dar: `extractEntities` opsiyonel `coveredEntities` / `args.entities` / `researchable` okuyor; alanı yalnız o üç araç üretiyor, diğer araçların dönüş şekli değişmiyor. Başarısız arama ve sonuçsuz sorgu kapsam bildirmiyor. Tanınmayan sembol adayları `unresolvedEntityTokens` olarak raporlanıyor — tahmin yürütülmüyor ama boşluk da sessizce yutulmuyor.

`resolveBistSymbol` bilinçli olarak kullanılmadı: serbest metinde `/^[A-Z]{3,6}$/` testiyle üç harfli her kelimeyi sembole çevirir ("son" → SON.IS).

## Aday hunisi sözleşmesi

`candidate-funnel.cjs` — **henüz hiçbir yere bağlı değil.** Kademe grameri, elenme gerekçe kodları ve `CANDIDATE_FUNNEL` kanıt nesnesi. Dört yapısal kural:

1. Sessiz eleme yasak — her elenen sembol gerekçe koduyla raporlanır
2. Gerekçe kodu kademeye bağlı — `SCORE_BELOW_THRESHOLD` uygunluk kademesinde yazılamaz
3. Veri yokluğu kalite hükmünden ayrı — kaynak limiti "kötü şirket" demek değil
4. Model listeyi değiştiremez — cevaptaki semboller huniyle karşılaştırılır

Kota doldurma yapısal olarak engellendi: `maxCandidates` tavan, hedef değil. Hiçbiri geçmezse `NO_CANDIDATE` geçerli sonuç.

**Eşik içermiyor, bilerek.** Likidite tabanı, havuz boyutu, skor ağırlıkları ve geçme notu politika dosyasından gelecek ve geriye dönük testle kalibre edilecek.

## Test

732 test (56 yeni), lint temiz. Yeni dosyalar: `candidate-funnel.test.mjs` (27), `bist-entity-resolver.test.mjs` (29), `voice-transcript-guards.test.mjs` (10), `bist-board-scope.test.mjs` (6).

## Bilinen sınırlar

- **Bu dal canlıda koşturulmadı** — birim testli, uygulama içinde doğrulanmadı. Özellikle entity düzeltmesinin sosyal kanıt alt sorusunu BLOCKED'dan çıkardığı görülmeli. Electron `.cjs` dosyalarını sıcak yüklemiyor; süreç yeniden başlatılmalı.
- Sürekli ritmik gürültü (masa tempo) hâlâ STT'ye gidiyor; tek öksürük artık eleniyor. Gerçek çözüm periyodiklik tespiti.
- Huninin kalan dört adımı ve önkoşulları README yol haritasında sıralı olarak yazılı. `CANDIDATE_FUNNEL` sonuç-duyarlı kanıt sınıfı üretimi yapılmadan statik `TOOL_EVIDENCE_CLASSES` tablosuna eklenmemeli — yoksa bloke tarama da kanıt üretmiş sayılır.

author: gdeaxx-pixel
body:
## Qué arregla

Los deploys quedan **stale**: Streamlit Cloud reescribe los archivos pero no siempre reinicia el proceso, así que `sys.modules` conserva el bytecode viejo y la app sirve código antiguo con archivos nuevos. Pasó en los deploys de #10 y #11 — las dos veces hubo que hacer **Reboot app** a mano.

Se reconoce porque el traceback mezcla los números de línea del archivo VIEJO con el texto del NUEVO.

## Por qué no se vigilan símbolos

El guardián de `app_old.py:31-41` se perdió en el corte al port. Miraba si a `logic` le faltaba algún símbolo de una lista escrita a mano. Ese enfoque falla de tres formas, las tres ya observadas:

1. **Solo ve símbolos nuevos.** Un arreglo dentro de una función existente es invisible. Contrastado contra los dos incidentes reales: habría detectado el #10 (trae `trg_real_data`), pero **no el #11** — su único símbolo nuevo era el helper privado `_tiene_datos`, que ninguna lista razonable habría incluido.
2. **Hay que alimentar la lista en cada PR** y nadie lo hace.
3. **Cubría 1 de los 10 módulos propios** que la app carga hoy (faltaban los 7 `ui.*` más `ui.nav` y `ui.tokens`).

Comparar la **fecha de modificación** no tiene ninguno de esos problemas: detecta cualquier cambio, no hay lista que mantener y los módulos se descubren solos recorriendo `sys.modules`.

## Cómo funciona

Tras los imports, `asegurar_frescura()` anota la fecha de cada archivo propio cargado. En las corridas siguientes las relee; si alguna se movió, recarga **todos** los módulos vigilados en orden de dependencias — quien hace `from otro import nombre` se queda con el nombre viejo aunque su archivo no se haya tocado.

Dos decisiones que no son obvias:
- La foto se toma **después** de los imports. Antes, una corrida posterior al despliegue registraría las fechas nuevas como suyas y no vería nada raro.
- El registro vive en el módulo, **no en `st.session_state`**: el estado de sesión nace vacío en cada visita y tendría el mismo punto ciego.

## Verificación

- **286 passed** (10 nuevos).
- El test central reproduce el patrón del #11: cambia el cuerpo, ningún símbolo nuevo.
- Un test **anti-rot** avisa si aparece un módulo propio sin sitio en el orden de recarga. Corre en subproceso porque dentro de pytest `sys.modules` acumula scripts que la app nunca importa (`fetch_roc_19a`, `validate_real_cases`).
- **Saboteado a propósito:** anulando la detección caen 5 tests; sacando `ui.vistas` del orden, cae el anti-rot.
- **Punta a punta** contra un módulo de sonda: un cambio de cuerpo se recoge sin reiniciar el proceso (`VERSION_A` → `VERSION_B`).
- App verificada en `localhost:8501` con `?demo=schwab2`: renderiza sin errores de consola.

## Ojo al mergear

Este despliegue **todavía puede llegar rancio** — el proceso que corre ahora no tiene el guardián cargado. Si al mergear la app se ve rara, un último **Reboot app**. De ahí en adelante ya no hace falta.

author: silverstein
body:
Partially addresses #130, which stays open for the automation half.

Publishing the Agent Plugin is a manual step, so the distribution repository lags this one until someone remembers. That is not hypothetical: #125 bounded decoded object-stream size, merged, and the published plugin kept serving the unfixed server until the drift was noticed by chance while checking something unrelated. Anyone installing during that window received the vulnerable build, with no signal that anything was stale.

## Why not the obvious check

Comparing the published commit to `HEAD` would fail after every merge and train everyone to ignore it. This compares only the paths the build actually copies into the artifact, so a docs or test commit stays quiet and a change under `server/` or `dist-ui/` does not.

## It found real drift on its first run

```
[freshness] STALE: the published plugin is missing 7 shipped file change(s) since 54f33e79:
  server/helpers.js
  server/index.js
  server/pdf-lib-worker.js
  server/qpdf-decrypt-worker.js
  server/qpdf-decrypt.js
  ...
```

#141 landed after the last publish. That is the same first-run result the publisher itself had when it was added, and it is the argument for automating this rather than remembering it.

## Deliberately not in the aggregate

It is expected to be red between a merge and a publish, and a gate that is routinely red is one people learn to merge past. Run it before publishing, or on a schedule.

## What is still missing

Closing the loop needs publish-on-merge, which needs a token with write access to the distribution repository. That is a credentials decision for a maintainer rather than something to assume, so #130 stays open for it.

author: athrvk
body:
## Description

**The plan.** Root cause: the per-tick series already contains every anomaly a run had (`latency_p99_ms`, the cumulative failure/completion counters, `current_rps`, the per-tick status map), and no code looks for them - `computeBreakpoint` is the only derived event, and it is SLO-relative and stops at the first crossing. So a 3-second collapse that recovered leaves the summary numbers almost unchanged and shows up only as a bump the reader has to spot. The approach: one pure detector over `LoadTestMetrics[]` (`detectAnomalies`), derived once per view and read twice - the charts shade the windows, the history Overview states them in words. **Rejected:** deriving inside `MetricsView`'s `DashboardDerived` bundle, which the issue suggests. That bundle deliberately depends on the latest tick and not on the history array (its comment says so), so folding a history-wide scan into it would rebuild it at 10 Hz and defeat the `React.memo` on `HeroRow` / `ModeStatsRow`. It is derived beside the other series transforms instead, which keeps the "no card re-derives from raw metrics" rule intact - the charts are the consumers and take it directly. **Also rejected:** teaching the chart layer about anomaly kinds. `plugins.ts` gets an `Annotation` (span + role + label) the way it already has a `Marker` (value + role + label), and `TimeSeriesCharts` maps the domain shape onto it beside the existing `breakpointMarker` helper.

Verified against the code before writing: every anchor in the issue still holds (`computeBreakpoint.ts:34-50`, `Marker`/`markersPlugin` at `plugins.ts:28-86`, `UPlotChartProps` markers wiring, `MetricsView`'s derived memo, `LoadTestDetail.tsx` recomputing the breakpoint from the fetched series).

**What lands:**

- **`detectAnomalies.ts`** - four rules, deliberately dumb and deterministic: latency spike (p99 past `3x` a trailing median of 15 ticks for `>= 2` consecutive ticks; the window stays open until p99 falls back under `1.5x`, with the baseline **frozen at the opening tick** so a long degradation cannot raise its own bar and report itself recovered), error burst (per-tick failure delta past 1% of that tick's completions - both counters are cumulative and are diffed), throughput drop (under 60% of the trailing median **while concurrency held**, so a ramp winding down is not an anomaly), and the first 5xx as a point. Windows are disjoint by construction, so there is no merge pass to go stale. Over 20 findings the list is triaged rather than truncated - the largest survive and the last one says how many did not. Every constant is exported and pinned by a test.
- **`annotationsPlugin`** (`plugins.ts`) - translucent bands from `startSeconds` to `endSeconds`, an instant drawn as a dashed rule, both clipped to the plot box so a zoomed-out window cannot paint over the axis. Registered before `markersPlugin` so the breakpoint's dashed rule stays legible over a band. `UPlotChart` takes `annotations` through the same ref-and-redraw path as `markers` (re-creating the plot would drop the user's zoom mid-run).
- **Live** (`MetricsView`): windows shade Throughput, Latency, Percentiles and Server Vitals over time.
- **History**: `LoadTestDetail` derives once and hands the result to both tabs - Performance shades the same charts, Overview renders a new **`RunEvents`** card (kind, the finding in words, the time range). Silent for a clean run: an "Events (0)" card puts the eye on the one thing with nothing to say.

No engine, storage or API change; a run with no findings and a run with no stored series both render exactly as before.

**Merged with master** after #490 and #492 landed - see [the resolution comment](https://github.com/athrvk/vayu/pull/494#issuecomment-5249283293). The notable half: #490's Server Vitals row now shades the same windows through the shared `BaseProps`, which is where the shading earns the most - "p99 spiked 4.2x at t=41" is answered right there by what the server was doing then.

## Type of Change
- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Documentation update

## Testing

`cd app && pnpm test && pnpm type-check && pnpm lint && pnpm format:check` - **3911 passed / 389 files** (22 new), type-check, ESLint and Prettier all clean, re-run after the master merge rather than only before it. No engine code is touched, so per root `CLAUDE.md` ("if no test could possibly go from green to red, do not run tests") the C++ suite was not run. No pre-existing failures observed.

Every rule is mutation-checked by actually reverting it and confirming red, not by inspection:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `LATENCY_SPIKE_FACTOR` 3 → 1 | 6 failed |
| `MIN_CONSECUTIVE_TICKS` 2 → 1 | 2 failed |
| read `requests_failed` undiffed | 2 failed |
| drop the concurrency guard | 1 failed |
| cap keeps insertion order instead of the largest | 1 failed |
| annotation band not clipped to the plot box | 1 failed |
| always draw a band, never a rule | 1 failed |
| draw offscreen windows | 1 failed |

The clean-run test is the one that could pass for the wrong reason, so its fixture drifts rather than sitting flat, and a companion test asserts the drift really does put consecutive ticks above the trailing median - i.e. the run is quiet *because of* the 3x factor, not because nothing in it could ever trip a rule. The plugin is driven directly against a recording 2D context rather than asserted through a rendered chart: jsdom has no layout and a stubbed context, so a mounted chart would pass just as happily with a plugin that drew nothing.

- [x] I have updated documentation

body:
Add per-family (ipv4/ipv6) "local ports" to NetworkConfig, parallel to the existing local addresses. A local port of 0 is treated as unset, in which case trackers fall back to reporting runtime::listen_port().

Announce requests now report the configured local port for the address family of the tracker connection instead of always using the listening port:
- HTTP trackers: the &port= query parameter (tracker_http.cc)
- UDP trackers: the port field of the announce packet (tracker_udp.cc)

Why: behind multiple layers of NAT, the port rtorrent is listening on is not the port other peers must reach the client at. Manually specifying the reported port per address family lets the client advertise the forwarded public port while still listening on the local one.
