Implements the ratified member-path design (#171). A member path is `<container><separator><member>`, and because the ecosystem uses several spellings - `!` (JAR / Java URLs), `#` (fragment style), the multi-character `!/` and `#/` other tools print, plus URI forms - the spelling is a presentation choice under user control rather than something hard-coded.

**`@xff_extras_api//:member_path_cc`** (`xff/archive/member_path.h`): `JoinMemberPath` / `SplitMemberPath` / `IsMemberPath` over `MemberPathOptions{separator, prefix}`. It lives in the shared API module because **both** sides need it - the archive extra renders member paths, the core parses one handed back in (a `-cmp` target, a `{def.X}`) - and an extra must not depend on the core.

**Flags:** `--archive-separator=STRING` (default `!`) and `--archive-prefix=none|uri`, registered globals with full detail text and a value table, gated on the archive extra exactly like `--archive`. `XFF.md` regenerated.

The rules that are *decisions* rather than implementation details each have a test:

| behaviour | why it is pinned |
| :------------------------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------- |
| plain concatenation - `a.tgz!/rooted`              | an absolute stored member keeps its slash; hiding it would hide the Zip-Slip red flag |
| `a.tgz!//rooted` under separator `!/`              | the doubled slash is correct, and is why plain `!` is the better default |
| split at the FIRST separator, remainder verbatim   | `a.tgz!weird!name` survives intact |
| empty separator never matches                      | otherwise every path is a member path with an empty container |
| `uri` refuses a bare path                          | the two spellings must never silently interchange |
| `Join` -> `Split` round-trip                       | across `!`, `#`, `!/`, `#/`, `::`, `/` crossed with relative / absolute / space-containing members |

**Verified:** the new test passes, `//...` is **94** tests green (was 93), `pre-commit run --all-files` clean, and the lean binary correctly answers `--archive-separator: this build has no archive support; rebuild with --//xff:xff_archive`. The flags appear in `--help=all` and in the committed `XFF.md`.

**Not yet done, deliberately:** the walk does not yet RENDER output through these flags - that arrives with the VFS backend - and the URI scheme is the generic `archive://` pending the per-format (`tar:` / `zip:`) decision, which TODO.md still lists as the one open sub-detail.

body:
Removes the last manual step from a release.

The device-flow login mints a Registry JWT that expires **five minutes** after
issue (decoded from the stored token on 2026-08-10), so a hand-run publish
401s with "token is expired" unless the login happened moments earlier. That is
what just happened cutting 0.12.0.

`mcp-publisher login github-oidc` needs no interaction and no new permission:
the job already declares `id-token: write` for PyPI trusted publishing.

Placement and retry are deliberate:

- After the PyPI publish, because the registry rejects a package version that
  is not live on PyPI, and PyPI serves new versions through a CDN.
- Last in the job, so a failure here leaves the PyPI and GitHub releases
  intact and recovery is one manual `mcp-publisher publish`, not a re-release.

The archive layout was checked rather than assumed: `LICENSE`, `README.md`,
`mcp-publisher` at the root of `mcp-publisher_linux_amd64.tar.gz`.

Untestable before merge by nature: the only way to exercise it is the next
release. If it fails there, the release itself still completes and the fallback
is the manual publish we have always done.

author: ajperel
body:
### Description
Fixes a bug where GCF v2 functions (such as kit functions) were loaded as duplicates in the existing backend state when the `dartfunctions` experiment was enabled.

The issue occurred because `loadCloudRunServices` swept all Cloud Run services (including GCF v2 services). Due to information loss in the Cloud Run v2 API list response (missing GCF annotations), the parser resolved GCF v2 services using their unprefixed/incorrect names, causing them to be added as duplicate endpoints.

To fix this, we implemented deduplication on load:
1. Expose the raw Cloud Run service ID in `endpoint.runServiceId` when parsing services in `src/gcp/runv2.ts`.
2. Update `loadCloudRunServices` in `src/deploy/functions/backend.ts` to check if the incoming service ID matches the `runServiceId` of any already loaded GCF v2 endpoint, and skip it if it matches.

#### Remaining Gap (functionsrunapionly)
Note that this load-side deduplication only works when the GCF API is called first (populating `existingBackend`). If the `functionsrunapionly` experiment is enabled, the GCF API is bypassed, and the parser will still resolve GCF v2 services with incorrect unprefixed names due to the missing annotations on Cloud Run.

To support kits in `functionsrunapionly` mode in the future, we will need to update the GCF v2 deploy path (`gcfV2.functionFromEndpoint` in `src/gcp/cloudfunctionsv2.ts`) to inject the `firebase-functions-metadata` annotation containing the prefixed ID during deployment, so that the Cloud Run parser can later resolve the correct prefixed name.

### Scenarios Tested
- Deploying kits (verified they no longer prompt for deletion of unprefixed functions).
- Deploying normal Node.js codebases.
- Deploying Dart (direct-to-run) codebases.
- Successfully ran all tests.

author: moabe-br-2019
body:
## The bug

`session login` closes the browser the moment `wait_seconds` runs out, with no special handling for a login that is still in progress. The budget was too small to cover a real human login with 2FA:

| caller | budget |
| --- | --- |
| CLI `session login` | 120s |
| MCP tool `bubble_session_login` | 180s |
| `capture_session_with_playwright` | 120s |

A password plus a 2FA code that arrives by email or SMS — with a retry if the first code expires — does not fit in two or three minutes. The window is killed mid-authentication and the capture fails.

This is not hypothetical: it is what happens on an account with 2FA enabled, every time.

## Why it surfaces now

Since #3, capture rejects anything that has not passed a real `calculate_derived` probe. So the timeout no longer yields a silently broken session that 401s later — it yields a hard failure. That is the correct behaviour, and I am not proposing to change it. But it does mean a user with 2FA cannot complete login at all, rather than getting a session that quietly misbehaves.

## The fix

Collapse the three budgets into one `DEFAULT_LOGIN_WAIT_SECONDS = 600` in `sessions/browser.py`, used by the CLI, the MCP tool and the capture helper.

This costs nothing on the happy path. The poll loop breaks as soon as the editor session validates, so a fast login still finishes in seconds — the larger budget is a ceiling, not a wait. Only a slow human path spends it.

Two supporting changes so the failure is legible if it ever happens again:

- The timeout error named no number and offered no remedy (`"Log in before the wait timeout expires."`). It now reports the budget that actually expired and points at `wait_seconds` / `--wait-seconds`.
- The tool schema explains that the budget covers the entire human flow including 2FA, so an agent calling the tool knows it is a knob worth raising.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/unit` — **639 passed, 14 failed**, identical to `main` on this machine. The 14 are pre-existing Windows failures unrelated to this change (6 symlink tests needing `SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege`, 5 `install_local`, plus `figma_bridge`, `language_registry` and `runtime_smoke`).
- [x] Updated the schema assertion in `test_mcp_server.py` to track the shared constant and to assert a floor (`>= 600`) rather than a magic number, so the budget cannot be silently shrunk back below what 2FA needs.
- [x] **Verified end to end against a real Bubble account with 2FA enabled.** The captured session carries `x-bubble-r: https://bubble.io/mfa`, confirming the MFA step was exercised and completed inside the window, and the capture only succeeded after `calculate_derived` validated it:

```
[bubble-mcp session] Waiting up to 600 seconds for session cookies.
[bubble-mcp session] Session cookies detected. Waiting for a validated editor session ...
[bubble-mcp session] Bubble editor session validated (calculate_derived succeeded).
[bubble-mcp session] Session capture complete: cookies saved, 20 Bubble header(s) captured.
```

## Note on a second failure mode

While tracing this I noticed that `_poll_browser_session` also exits through a bare `except Exception: break` (`sessions/browser.py`), which closes the browser with no log at all. If Playwright raises during one of the navigations in the login flow, the symptom is indistinguishable from a timeout for the user. I left it out of this PR to keep the change focused, but it is worth a follow-up: at minimum the exception should be surfaced rather than swallowed.

author: realtonyyoung
body:
Fixes three independent CI flake mechanisms. All fixes are root-cause fixes in test/CI infrastructure — no production code changes, no wait-budget inflation.

## 1. `--maximum-parallel-tests 1` never serialized the keyed phase (empty-sink funnel failures + device-id timestamp flake)

TUnit's `TestScheduler` applies the global cap only to the *parallel bucket*; keyed `[NotInParallel("key")]` tests go through `ConstraintKeyScheduler.ExecuteTestsWithConstraintsAsync`, which starts every test whose keys are free **without consulting the cap** (verified against TUnit 1.18.37 source). Tests with disjoint key sets therefore run concurrently even on CI.

`ConfigSetTelemetryCompositionTests` held only the `TokenStoreProfileTests` key while driving the real `config set telemetry off` path:

- `TelemetryState.SetEnabled(false)` → `TelemetryDeviceId.Delete()` dereferences whatever `TelemetryDeviceId.PathOverride` points at *the instant it runs* — mid-flight, that's the concurrently-running telemetry-keyed test's private file. That is the `Second_get_or_create_does_not_rewrite_file_when_id_exists` failure (#524): the sidecar really was deleted and re-created (with a fresh GUID), not an mtime-resolution artifact.
- `CliTelemetry.DiscardAndDisable()` clears the live `TestSink` and flips `Enabled` — the `SetupFunnelTests` "collection has 0 items but expected 2" / "Expected 12 but found 0" failures, where `AssertEnabled` passes at test start and the emit sites provably execute (the failing run's own stderr shows the zero-tenant dead-end message) yet the sink ends empty.

Fix: the class now holds the two telemetry lock keys alongside the config-dir key, and its class doc explains why (the old doc's "left unset, both fall back to their own defaults" reasoning missed that the production path dereferences the *live* overrides). Evidence: a TRX timing run on the unfixed code showed a `ConfigSetTelemetryCompositionTests` test overlapping a telemetry-keyed test on the very first attempt; post-fix runs show zero cross-lane overlaps (guaranteed by the shared key, not luck).

The ci.yml comment claiming the flag "serializes the entire unit suite" is corrected so nobody trusts it to prevent this class of race again.

## 2. Silent best-effort cleanup of the seeded `default`-profile token

#521 (already on main) fixed the `NotAuthenticated_MakesNoRequest_AndReturnsZero` victim side: the stale provider-cache entry on a reused WireMock port plus per-test token/profile clearing. This PR hardens the one remaining *seeder*: `McpFlowsServerTests.CleanupDefaultToken` swallowed every delete failure, so one transient Windows sharing violation leaves a VALID `default`-profile token that makes any later default-profile-resolving test authenticate for real. The cleanup now retries transient sharing violations and then throws naming the leak, instead of silently leaving the poison behind.

## 3. Consent harness timer counter rose before the timer existed (`Timed out waiting for: the resubscribe`, #523)

`TimerCountingTimeProvider.CreateTimer` incremented its counter **before** calling `inner.CreateTimer`. `ConsentHarness.RetryAsync` uses that counter as the "retry delay is armed" signal before advancing the fake clock — so a preemption between the increment and FakeTimeProvider's internal registration let the test thread `Advance(1s)` while the timer didn't exist yet. The delay then got scheduled one second into a future nothing ever advances to, and the wait for the resubscribe timed out after 5s. Preemption-sized window ⇒ rare, loaded-Windows-runner-biased, passes on rerun — exactly the observed shape. `ConsentService` has exactly one timer consumer of the injected `TimeProvider` (the retry delay), so no other mechanism was in play.

Fix: register with the fake first, increment after.

## Verification

- Telemetry namespace (152 tests): pre-fix TRX run demonstrated the cross-lane overlap; 3 post-fix TRX rounds green with zero overlaps; 30-loop soak green.
- `McpFlowsServerTests` 52/52, `ReportVersionCommandTests` (main's #521 version) 12/12, `AuthProviderCacheIsolationTests` 2/2, `ConsentServiceTests` 25/25 (×5 pre-rebase).
- `scripts/check-linear-ids.sh` clean.

Closes #523
Closes #524

body:
A customer opened **ASA713** — an Alaska flight — and the card drew a **United 737-9**, with nothing on screen saying the picture was of the *type* rather than of that aircraft.

The data was correct: the proxy sent `pk: "type"` and the device received it. The caption that said so got moved to the **data page** during the callsign-only full-bleed redesign, with the other category-descriptive fields.

That reasoning — *"the photo replaces the fields that describe the category"* — holds for a Cessna. It does not hold for an airliner, because every airliner stock photo is a real aircraft in a real operator's scheme. **Nine types in the library wear United livery alone** (B77W, B39M, A319, A21N, B772, B78X, B753…), so any Alaska/Delta/Southwest flight of those types shows the same mismatch.

**Read a livery and you read identity, not category.** That's the one field a photograph cannot replace, whatever else it replaces.

Costs no pixels: the hint line is drawn either way, and `tap: details` is the most redundant text on the card — every other screen teaches the tap. A per-airframe photo (`pk: "hex"`) *is* that aircraft, so it keeps the hint and stays uncaptioned.

Builds clean on `blipscope-s3-128`. Not yet flashed — it goes on COM119 together with the framing change from #222 so both are judged on the glass in one go.

The engine can now *consume* a classpath. Obtaining one from a real Gradle multi-module build (via the Tooling API) is the untested half of the §8 risk and the last item before the gate fully closes — tracked in the plan, next branch.
